utterances.text: -- and at Ovcara? How many people were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: There was one in Velepromet, and there were two at Ovcara, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything at all about the fact that the JNA did not participate in what happened at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I could not -- I -- I don't know. I -- I don't have an answer for that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's fine. If you can't answer, you can't. But apart from the fact that Major Sljivancanin was in command of the JNA in Vukovar at the time of the attack on Vukovar, apart from that fact, is there any other fact that could link him up to the events at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's really not for the witness to say. I mean, he can say what he saw and heard. You saw Sljivancanin beside the bus or beside the buses, you said. You saw him outside the hanger, but you didn't see him inside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And you saw him earlier at Velepromet. Was there any other sightings during the day or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Velepromet, the barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The barracks, yes. Your last question, Mr. Milosevic, because your time is up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it's the last question, then here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have a document showing the reasons for which you were released from the JNA when you were released from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I was -- it was on my request because of a lot of stress that I went through. No, I don't have a document. No, I'm sorry. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in your statement you said the following: That at one point in time you heard a heated discussion between Stanko Vujanovic and Miro Vujovic with officers of the JNA, including Sljivancanin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in this heated discussion, did you hear what Sljivancanin actually said or not? Did you hear a single word uttered by Sljivancanin in that heated argument?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Sir, if you could turn to the end of your statement, there are three hand-drawn maps and I would like you to take a look at number 3, which is marked Ovcara. Just a quick question. You mentioned that you saw Major Sljivancanin outside the hangar. Have you -- first of all, did you draw this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And have you marked on this map exactly where it was that you saw Major Sljivancanin standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: Just before the entrance of -- into hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: There's -- at the bottom of the page before the road, it says Sljivancanin with a few more military, and there's a circle just above that. Is that circle where you saw Major Sljivancanin standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Turning back to your statement, in paragraph 9 you were -- and 10 -- well, actually before that. You were asked, first of all, about when you were beaten by some people because you were wearing a JNA uniform. You said they were wearing civilian clothes. Do you know whether or not those people were actually civilians or whether they were members of some Croatian army or officials of the Croatian government in some fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I -- I don't really know. I don't have any connections to that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions about harassing telephone calls that you received before you left Vukovar, and that's in paragraph 6 of your statement. Do you know whether the people that were making those telephone calls were officials making them in some official capacity as officials of the government or members of the army or whether these were just individual citizens or don't you know who was making them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I didn't know who was making those calls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Now, when you -- you left Belgrade -- or you left Vukovar to go to Belgrade, you said, because you were afraid of what was happening. Do you know whether or not Croatians were also leaving Vukovar at the time because they were afraid also -- or I'm sorry, Serbians were leaving because they were afraid of what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: We heard a couple of cases that people were leaving, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And were Croats leaving as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I heard that too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Now, you were asked whether or not you had any harassment or anyone mistreated you because of your former surname, and you said -- you answered no, they didn't because you had someone protecting you. Is that person who was protecting you the person that you've referred to in your statement who rescued you from the Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: When you were being questioned at the Velepromet after you were kidnapped and taken there from Sid, were you harassed there because of your surname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: The people that were questioning you there and holding you there for two days, were they individual citizens unaffiliated with the military or were these official members of the military forces such as the JNA or the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I believe they were the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Do you know what the Velepromet was used for during this part of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I believe there was some kind of military warehouse, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: You were asked whether or not your stepfather who went with you to Belgrade was harassed because he was a non-Serb and you answered that he wasn't. How about when you were questioned by -- by the members of the Territorial Defence in the Velepromet? Did they ask you any questions about your stepfather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: No. No, I don't recall. Maybe they did. I'm not really sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: You said at the Velepromet, turning now ahead in time to the 19th and 20th, you were asked by the accused whether the people there were interrogated and released and you answered yes. Was everyone who was interrogated immediately released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: What about your grandfather and grandmother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: No. They spent a couple days over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And where were they sent from the Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: To gaol in Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Okay. At some point before they were released from Sremska Mitrovica, were they sent somewhere else and made to engage in forced labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: Not that I recall of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: You were -- finally, you were asked about why it was that your protector was looking for his parents who were hiding in a basement in Vukovar. During the conflict, was it possible to go from the neighbourhood that you were staying in, Petrova Gora, back and forth to the main area in Vukovar where people were hiding in cellars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: No, it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: How far is it from Petrova Gora to the centre of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I would say around four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And when you came into Vukovar on the 20th of November, could you just, in a sentence, describe what the condition was of the city.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: It was terrible. It was -- you couldn't recognise the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Now, the area of Petrova Gora, is that an area that's predominantly Croatian or Serbian residents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: I would say Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And what was the condition of Petrova Gora on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-006
utterances.text: It was pretty much intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: That's all I have, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness C-006, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We're very grateful. May that witness be taken now rather than a 92 bis witness? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, provided there's time to get through his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome is going to take him briefly. He confirms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.
